title: Rabbi Yose ben Perida
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Yose ben Perida. The beloved disciple of Rabbi Eliezer, as in [Eruvin 11b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.11b.28). Hyman quotes the [Tosefta there, chapter 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Eruvin.1.2): “An incident in which Rabbi Eliezer went to Rabbi Yose ben Perora, his disciple, at Ublin. He said to him, ‘My son,’” and so on. In the [Yerushalmi there, chapter 1, halakha 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.1.2.2), he is called “Yose ben Yose ben Perora.”

notes.text: The heading Perida and the body’s Perora differ; the last citation doubles Yose. Ublin is left unidentified and is not rendered as the Polish city Lublin. These source questions remain open.

The linked Yerushalmi edition has one Yose: Yose ben Perorah. The Venice witness has the doubled form quoted by Hyman. In the Bavli, the account [continues on 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.12a.1) with Eliezer’s address, “My son.”

Eruvin 11b ends by naming Yose ben Perida, Rabbi Eliezer’s disciple. At the start of 12a, the story continues at Ovelin and includes the address “My son.” The consulted Tosefta Eruvin 1 has “[Yosef] ben Perida” at Ublin and omits “his disciple” in this passage. The Venice Yerushalmi Eruvin 1:2 calls him Yose ben Yose ben Perorah and calls him Eliezer’s disciple. Hyman’s heading Perida and the Perora of his quotation are kept as printed. Ublin remains unidentified.
